A polite host phrase for a guest.

exercises.prompt: A close friend arrives at your flat. Warmly say: “Come in, come in!”
exercises.explanation: With a friend, use the informal command «entra». Learn «Entra, entra!» as one welcoming chunk.

exercises.prompt: An older neighbour is at the door. Politely say: “Please come in.”
exercises.explanation: «Faz favor de entrar» is a polite fixed phrase for inviting someone inside. Learn it whole.

exercises.prompt: Your female friend answers: «Sim, obrigada.» Ask her (informal) if she wants something to drink.
exercises.explanation: For a friend, use the fixed host phrase «Queres beber alguma coisa?». It is a very common offer at home.

exercises.prompt: Your older female guest answers: «Sim, um bocadinho, por favor.» Ask her (formal) if she wants a little more cake.
exercises.explanation: To offer more food politely, use «Quer mais um bocadinho de…?». Here the noun in the prompt tells you it is cake.
acceptedAnswers: A senhora quer mais um bocadinho de bolo?

exercises.prompt: The guest is a woman. Fill the host’s offer and the guest’s polite refusal.
exercises.explanation: «Mais um bocadinho?» is a common offer at the table. The guest is a woman, so she says «já estou satisfeita», not «satisfeito».
exercises.template:
— ___ um bocadinho de bolo?
— Não, obrigada. Já estou ___.

exercises.prompt: You loved the dinner (o jantar). Tell your host: “It was great!”
exercises.explanation: The adjective agrees with the thing you praise, not with you: «o jantar» is masculine, so «Estava ótimo!». About «a sopa» you would say «Estava ótima!».

exercises.prompt: Thank your host for the invitation. The speaker’s gender is not important.
exercises.explanation: The whole phrase is fixed; only «obrigado / obrigada» changes with the speaker. Both forms are accepted here.

exercises.prompt: Invite a friend to visit you another day. Say: “Come round to my place sometime.”
exercises.explanation: «Aparece lá em casa» is an informal invitation you can learn as one chunk. It sounds friendly and natural in Portugal.

exercises.prompt: A friend invites you out, but you cannot go. First say: “Unfortunately I can’t.”
exercises.explanation: «Infelizmente não posso» is a useful polite refusal. You can add another sentence after it, but this chunk works on its own.

exercises.prompt: After declining an invitation, soften it with: “Maybe next time.”
exercises.explanation: «Fica para a próxima» is a fixed phrase that keeps the tone friendly after saying no.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Claro, em que posso ajudar?» Ask them (informal) if they can give you a hand.
exercises.explanation: «Podes dar-me uma ajuda?» is a very common informal way to ask for a small favour. Learn it as a whole expression.

exercises.prompt: An older neighbour answers: «Sim, diga.» Ask him (formal) if he has a minute.
exercises.explanation: To get someone’s attention politely before a request, use «Tem um minuto?». You may also say «O senhor tem um minuto?».

exercises.prompt: You need help with a heavy box. Fill the polite informal question.
exercises.explanation: The useful chunk is «Importas-te de me ajudar?». Here the extra words say what you need help with.
exercises.template: ___-te de me ajudar com esta caixa?

exercises.prompt: You want to tell a friend «Don't trouble yourself.» One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With «tu», the set phrase is «Não te incomodes.». Learn the whole chunk for saying “don’t bother”.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The natural fixed phrase is «Não é incómodo nenhum.». «Alguma» does not work here.

exercises.prompt: Someone rings your doorbell and you shout from inside: “I’m coming!”
exercises.explanation: Portuguese often uses the short chunk «Já vou!» in this situation. It is the normal thing to call out from inside the house.

exercises.prompt: Your friend next door is studying. Apologise informally for the noise.
exercises.explanation: For a friend or someone your age, use «Desculpa o barulho». The phrase is best learned whole.
exercises.template: ___ o barulho, estamos a arrumar a sala.

exercises.prompt: Answer with a phrase you can really use.
exercises.explanation: «Fica à vontade» is a very common host phrase. Learn it as one chunk for making a guest feel comfortable.
exercises.question: Quando recebes um amigo em casa, o que dizes para ele ficar à vontade?

exercises.prompt: A guest arrives at a home. Put the mini-dialogue in order.
exercises.explanation: The guest comes in, asks about the shoes, sits down, and then the host offers a drink. Listen for the natural order of actions at home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boa tarde! A porta está aberta.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Obrigada. Posso deixar os sapatos aqui?

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the words in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Sirva-se» is a polite fixed phrase meaning “help yourself”. Learn it as a chunk, without analysing the grammar yet.

exercises.prompt: A friend arrives and stays standing in the hall. Tell them politely to sit down.
exercises.explanation: Use the informal form with a friend. This is a common hosting phrase at home.

exercises.prompt: An older neighbour comes in. Invite them to sit down politely.
exercises.explanation: With an older guest, use the formal form. Learn this as a fixed polite phrase.

exercises.prompt: Your older neighbour answers: «Um chá, se faz favor.» Ask politely, using the phrase from this set, whether she would like something to drink.
exercises.explanation: For a polite offer, use the 3rd-person form «quer». The phrase is a useful whole chunk for hosting.
acceptedAnswers: A senhora quer beber alguma coisa?

exercises.prompt: Your friend has just arrived at your home after work. Offer something to eat.
exercises.explanation: This is the informal version because you are speaking to a friend. It offers food in a general way.

exercises.prompt: You are offering some food politely to an older guest. Complete the phrase.
exercises.explanation: This is a useful polite table phrase. Learn the whole expression together.

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks when they can come round another day. Say: 'Whenever you want.'
exercises.explanation: This short phrase keeps the invitation open and friendly. Use it with someone you know well.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Sim, posso passar aí no sábado.» Ask him, using the phrase from this set, if he wants to come over to your place.
exercises.explanation: Use the informal question because you are speaking to a friend. The phrase «cá a casa» means to your home.
exercises.givenAnswer: Sim, posso passar aí no sábado.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: In European Portuguese, «bathroom» is «casa de banho». This is the normal phrase to use in someone's home.

exercises.prompt: You are visiting someone's home and need the bathroom. Ask politely.
exercises.explanation: This is the normal polite question in a home. In Portugal, use «casa de banho», not Brazilian «banheiro».
acceptedAnswers: Posso ir à casa de banho?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: For the state of a door, Portuguese uses «estar»: «A porta está aberta.»

exercises.prompt: Someone rings the bell, but the door is already unlocked. Call out: “The door is open.”
exercises.explanation: Use «estar» for the state of the door. This phrase tells the visitor they can come in straight away.

exercises.prompt: Your host answers: «Sim, podes deixá-los aqui.» Ask, using the phrase from this set, if you can leave your shoes here.
exercises.explanation: This is a practical question when you visit someone's home. Learn the full phrase as one chunk.

exercises.prompt: You are offering a simple choice of drinks. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: This is a very common host phrase. Use «ou» to offer a choice between two things.

exercises.prompt: Your friend has finished the first cup. Offer more tea.
exercises.explanation: With a friend, use the informal form «queres». «Mais» adds the idea of another amount.

exercises.prompt: An older guest has finished the first cup. Offer more coffee politely.
exercises.explanation: Because the guest is older, use the formal form «quer». This is a short, natural hosting phrase.

exercises.prompt: You want to tell an older neighbour «Don't trouble yourself.» One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With «o senhor / a senhora», the polite form is «Não se incomode.». «Incomodas» is a «tu» form. Learn it as a fixed phrase.

exercises.prompt: You are hosting an older guest. Complete the polite phrase meaning 'Make yourself at home.'
exercises.explanation: This is a formal host phrase. Learn «A casa é sua» as one chunk.

exercises.prompt: You are leaving your neighbour's flat and you will meet again tomorrow. Say: “We'll see each other tomorrow.”
exercises.explanation: Use this fixed phrase when the next meeting is already tomorrow, not just sometime soon.

exercises.prompt: Your friend is going home after dinner. Ask them to give your regards to the family.
exercises.explanation: With a friend, use the informal form «manda». «À família» uses the contraction «a + a = à».

exercises.prompt: Your older neighbour answers: «Claro, já a abro.» Ask politely, using the phrase from this set, if they can open the window.
exercises.explanation: For a polite small favour, use the formal form «pode». This is a useful home phrase to learn as a chunk.
acceptedAnswers: O senhor pode abrir a janela?
A senhora pode abrir a janela?
